title: Kubernetes
tagline: Go from your first cluster and deployment to networking, security, scaling and running clusters yourself.

credit.text: Based on the Kubernetes roadmap from roadmap.sh (personal use)

phases.title: Introduction
phases.description: Learn what Kubernetes is, the vocabulary it uses and how containers fit underneath it.

phases.title: Setting up Kubernetes
phases.description: Get a cluster running locally or with a managed provider and deploy something to it.

phases.title: Running applications
phases.description: Know the main workload objects and when each one is the right fit.

phases.title: Services and networking
phases.description: Expose workloads, balance traffic and understand how pods talk to each other.

phases.title: Configuration management
phases.description: Feed settings and secrets into pods without baking them into images.

phases.title: Resource management
phases.description: Control how much CPU and memory workloads and namespaces may use and keep an eye on it.

phases.title: Security
phases.description: Lock down who can do what in the cluster, what traffic is allowed and how containers run.

phases.title: Monitoring and logging
phases.description: Collect logs, metrics and traces so you can see the health of what runs in the cluster.

phases.title: Autoscaling
phases.description: Scale pods sideways or upwards and grow the cluster itself as load changes.

phases.title: Scheduling
phases.description: Influence where pods land and which ones win when the cluster runs short.

phases.title: Storage and volumes
phases.description: Attach persistent storage and run stateful applications reliably.

phases.title: Deployment patterns
phases.description: Automate releases with CI/CD, GitOps and Helm and roll out changes safely.

phases.title: Advanced topics
phases.description: Extend Kubernetes with your own resources and controllers and learn to operate clusters yourself.
items: Should you manage your own Cluster
